items.e: Malnutrition increases PJI risk when serum albumin is below 3.5 g/dL (or transferrin < 200, lymphocytes < 1,500). Significant modifiable risk factors include HbA1c > 7.5-8%, BMI > 40 kg/m², and intra-articular corticosteroid injection within 3 months prior to arthroplasty.
items.note: Clear, single best answer testing well-defined, consensus-based preoperative risk thresholds.

items.q: Which of the following therapeutic principles regarding antimicrobial management in periprosthetic joint infection is supported by findings from recent clinical trials?
o: Six weeks of antibiotic therapy achieved superior infection control compared to 12 weeks in the DATIPO trial
Rifampicin monotherapy is recommended for eradicating staphylococcal biofilm on well-fixed implants
Oral antibiotic therapy was non-inferior to intravenous therapy within the first 6 weeks of treatment in the OVIVA trial
Continuous intravenous therapy for 12 weeks is mandatory for all fungal and Gram-negative infections
items.e: The 2019 OVIVA trial demonstrated that oral antibiotic therapy was non-inferior to intravenous therapy within the first 6 weeks for bone and joint infections (including PJI) with fewer line-related complications. In contrast, the 2021 DATIPO trial demonstrated that 12 weeks of antibiotics was superior to 6 weeks for PJI, and rifampicin must never be used as monotherapy due to rapid resistance emergence.
items.note: Tests key evidence-based practice changes from major recent trials (OVIVA and DATIPO).

items.q: A 66-year-old man presents with acute knee pain, high fever, and effusion 3 years after an uneventful total knee arthroplasty. Symptoms began abruptly 4 days ago after a dental abscess. Radiographs confirm that all components remain well-fixed. Synovial aspiration yields methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA). The soft-tissue envelope is healthy without a sinus tract. If a debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) procedure is undertaken, which surgical and pharmacological strategy is essential?
o: Retention of the original polyethylene insert to preserve ligament balance, combined with linezolid monotherapy
Exchange of all modular parts (polyethylene insert) along with addition of rifampicin to the pathogen-specific antibiotic regimen
Retention of all modular components, combined with 6 weeks of intravenous aminoglycoside monotherapy
In situ drilling of the femoral component with application of high-dose vancomycin powder without modular exchange
items.e: For an acute haematogenous infection (symptoms < 3 weeks) with well-fixed implants and intact soft tissues, DAIR is indicated. Complete synovectomy with exchange of all modular components (polyethylene insert/modular heads) is an essential surgical step, and rifampicin should be added to the pathogen-specific antibiotic regimen for its biofilm-active properties against staphylococci.
items.note: Standard surgical management question testing modular component exchange and biofilm-active antibiotic therapy.

items.q: A patient undergoes revision total hip arthroplasty after complete wear-through of a conventional polyethylene liner, resulting in the femoral head articulating directly against the metallic acetabular shell. According to McKellop's classification, this mechanism represents which mode of wear?
items.e: According to McKellop's classification, Mode 2 wear occurs when an intended primary bearing surface articulates against a non-intended secondary surface, such as a femoral head rubbing against the acetabular shell after liner wear-through.
items.note: Accurate, standard question mapping directly to McKellop's wear modes.

items.q: In the biology of wear particle-induced periprosthetic osteolysis around joint replacements, which polyethylene particle size range is biologically most active in phagocytosis and macrophage activation?
items.e: Polyethylene wear particles in the 0.1 to 1.0 micron size range are the most biologically active, triggering macrophage phagocytosis and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-alpha and RANKL.
items.note: Standard arthroplasty biology fact; clear distractors and unambiguous correct option.

items.q: During the manufacturing of highly cross-linked polyethylene (HXLPE), what is the primary consequence of post-irradiation thermal remelting above its melting point (approximately 135–137°C)?
o: Preservation of crystallinity but persistence of residual free radicals
Complete elimination of free radicals at the expense of fatigue strength and toughness
Quenching of free radicals without altering yield strength or crystallinity
Increased resistance to fatigue crack propagation and delamination
items.e: Post-irradiation remelting above the melting point eliminates free radicals and prevents oxidation, but it decreases polymer crystallinity, fatigue strength, and fracture toughness. In contrast, annealing below the melting point preserves mechanical properties but leaves residual free radicals.
items.note: Tests a core polymer engineering principle critical for choosing bearings in THA vs TKA.

items.q: A patient with a metal-on-polyethylene total hip arthroplasty presents with an adverse local tissue reaction (ALTR). Which serum metal ion pattern is most indicative of mechanically assisted crevice corrosion (trunnionosis) rather than bearing surface wear?
o: Co:Cr ratio near 1:1 with equivalent elevation of both ions
Isolated elevation of chromium with normal cobalt levels
Co:Cr ratio greater than 3 to 5 with cobalt elevation exceeding chromium
Isolated elevation of titanium ions without cobalt or chromium release
items.e: Mechanically assisted crevice corrosion at the head-neck taper selectively releases cobalt into the circulation. A cobalt-to-chromium ratio greater than approximately 3 to 5 is diagnostic of taper corrosion (trunnionosis) rather than bearing wear.

items.q: In the tribology of total joint arthroplasty, full fluid-film lubrication is established when the lambda ratio (ratio of lubricant film thickness to composite surface roughness) is:
items.e: A lambda ratio exceeding 3 denotes full fluid-film lubrication, where the fluid layer entirely separates articulating asperities to minimise abrasive wear. items.e: The osteolysis threshold established by Dumbleton for conventional polyethylene is approximately 0.1 mm/year of linear wear; wear rates exceeding this threshold are strongly associated with progressive periprosthetic osteolysis.
items.note: Classic landmark value in arthroplasty tribology tested regularly in superspeciality exams.

items.q: A patient with a failed metal-on-metal hip prosthesis and markedly elevated serum cobalt levels presents with cardiomyopathy, peripheral neuropathy, and hearing loss. Which endocrine abnormality is recognized as a manifestation of systemic cobalt toxicity?
items.e: Systemic cobalt toxicity resulting from excessive metal wear or corrosion can manifest clinically with cardiomyopathy, peripheral neuropathy, sensorineural hearing loss, visual impairment, and hypothyroidism.
items.note: High-yield systemic complication of cobaltism described in regulatory warnings and Campbell's.

items.q: A 68‑year‑old man presents 5 years after a primary total hip arthroplasty with progressive groin pain and a palpable lump over the superior pubic ramus.
